purpose: Close the gap where the canonical email rule matched nothing at all when the local part is a single character, so addresses like a@b.co and x@mail.ru travelled completely unmasked on all three channels that share maskText - the access-log middleware, the global logger, and the Sentry outbound handler. Verified by running maskText, not by reading the regex: a@b.co came back untouched while ab@b.co became a***@b.co.
requiredInvariants: One rule is added; no existing rule, field name, class or exported symbol is modified. The existing email rule keeps its pattern and its replacement.

Only one-character local parts change behaviour. Verified against origin/main by running the pre-change rule set over the same corpus: ab@b.co, a.b@x.com, ivan.petrov@example.com and user_1@sub.domain.co.uk all produce byte-identical output before and after, and the spec pins each of them.
The local part is removed entirely rather than partially masked. Keeping a prefix is meaningless when the prefix is the whole local part, which is why partial masking is not the fix here.
The domain is preserved, consistent with every other rule in the set.

The new rule is placed after the existing email rule. Placed before it, it would strip the last character of a long local part instead of leaving that address to the main rule; the spec pins this ordering.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database mutation, and no business logic change.
acceptance: The spec guard that requires a VALUE_SAMPLES entry for every rule is satisfied - it failed first without one, which is how the new rule was caught as unverified.
src/common/security passes 81/81 and the full API suite passes with no regressions.
